title: Your worst piece
line: Find the piece doing the least, and give it a better square.

steps.text: Before a quiet move, ask which of your pieces does the least. Here it is Black's knight on a5, out on the edge.
Tap every square the knight on a5 can move to.
steps.hint: A knight jumps two squares one way and one square to the side.
steps.after: Only four squares, and from the edge it guards nothing in the center.

steps.text: Bring the knight back toward the middle, where it hits White's center pawn.

also.c8d7: That is as good. This lesson first moves the knight, the worst piece.

steps.after: White pushes a pawn to keep your knight out of b4.

steps.text: Count again. Tap every square the knight can move to now.
steps.after: More squares, and it presses on the center.

steps.text: Now the piece doing the least is the bishop still at home. Bring it out one square.
steps.after: The bishop joins the game, and the rook behind it can come out later.

summary: Find your piece doing the least and give it a better square. A knight on the edge is often the one.
